cutoff_window.date_policy: Only a public source with a visible, unambiguous timestamp inside this strict 48-hour window qualifies. NVD publication times establish public-record disclosure timing, not exploit, exposure, or remediation timing.

qualifying_findings.title: Vikunja bot-user API tokens retain access after the corresponding human user is disabled or locked
qualifying_findings.topic: identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public-record disclosure with a linked upstream GitHub Security Advisory. The NVD timestamp is the qualifying in-window date; fixed-release details require direct advisory confirmation at synthesis.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD published a Vikunja 2.4.0 through before 2.7.1 authentication-bypass record: token validation checks a bot user's status rather than the disabled or locked human user's status, so holders of pre-minted bot tokens can continue reading and modifying shared projects through HTTP API, CalDAV, MCP, and feeds.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Bot-owned API-token validation across Vikunja API, CalDAV, MCP, and feed boundaries; affected 2.4.0 to before 2.7.1.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP-connected agent or integration using a bot token can retain delegated authority after the human principal is disabled, violating revocation and least-privilege expectations.

upstream_routing.note: Vikunja product context remains ai-wiki-owned; this repository owns the token-revocation and MCP delegated-authority implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence: High for the public-record description and affected range; medium for the exact upgrade/remediation guidance until the primary advisory is reconciled.

qualifying_findings.title: Vikunja project metadata prompt injection into a coding agent's authoritative instruction block
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public-record disclosure with a linked upstream GitHub Security Advisory. The NVD timestamp is the qualifying in-window date.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD published a Vikunja before 2.7.1 prompt-injection record: a project member with write access can place instructions in project titles or task content that a prime hook renders verbatim in a coding agent's authoritative instruction block on SessionStart and PreCompact, potentially steering checkout modifications or command execution.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Project-title and task-description ingestion into a coding-agent instruction block; affected before 2.7.1.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Untrusted collaboration metadata crosses into high-trust prompt context and can influence autonomous developer-tool actions; provenance labelling and instruction/data separation are relevant controls.

upstream_routing.note: General coding-agent workflow discussion belongs in ai-dev-wiki; the prompt trust-boundary vulnerability and security controls are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence: High for the NVD-described trust boundary and affected range; medium for deployment-specific impact because the record describes a particular hook integration.

qualifying_findings.title: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway tool-name collision denial of service
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public-record disclosure with a linked vendor IBM Support advisory. The NVD timestamp is the qualifying in-window date.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD published an IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway 1.0.0 through 1.0.11 vulnerability: improper slug normalization can cause tool-name collisions, allowing a remote authenticated attacker to cause denial of service.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ContextForge MCP Gateway tool-name normalization; versions 1.0.0 through 1.0.11; authenticated remote attack precondition.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Gateway tool naming is part of an agent's capability-routing boundary. Collisions can turn a permitted authenticated request into availability loss for MCP-connected agent operations.

upstream_routing.note: IBM and ContextForge catalog background remains ai-wiki-owned; the MCP gateway availability boundary is locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence: High for product, versions, authentication precondition, and stated denial-of-service impact; remediation details require the vendor advisory at synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenBMB Internet of Agents message, registry, and collaboration-layer access and resource-control flaws
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Three NVD public-record disclosures with linked public upstream issue reports. NVD dates qualify the group; records state that the project had not responded, so no fixed release is claimed.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD published three Internet of Agents records affecting revisions through commit 9d78e88e47160eb42ee1ee8538c05e1c2c47877a: CVE-2026-123881 permits remote improper access control through the message handler's comm_id; CVE-2026-123963 describes missing authentication in agent registration through desc/name; and CVE-2026-123964 permits a remote infinite-loop denial of service through collaboration-layer max_turns.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenBMB Internet of Agents im_server/app.py message and registry functions plus im_client collaboration-layer launch_goal; affected through commit 9d78e88e47160eb42ee1ee8538c05e1c2c47877a; no unaffected release identified by the records.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: These findings cover core multi-agent trust boundaries: message-record access, agent enrollment authentication, and bounded autonomous collaboration. Deployments should not infer a fix from the disclosure alone.

upstream_routing.note: Internet of Agents framework background remains ai-wiki-owned; authentication, authorization, and autonomous-loop security implications are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence: Medium-high for the disclosed components and effects; medium for remediation state because the records provide commit-based scope and cite unresolved upstream reports.
